units.text: Amazon CloudFront delivers content from locations closer to viewers. Those locations are called edges. A shopper in Asia requests a product photo. On a cache hit, the edge already has a usable copy and returns it without going back to the origin. On a miss, CloudFront checks upstream and fetches the original from S three if needed.
The time to live sets how long a copy stays fresh, based on cache settings and origin headers. After that, CloudFront can check for a current copy.

The origin supplies the content. Use an S three bucket for files like product photos. For requests that need a running web app, CloudFront can route to an Application Load Balancer instead. H T T P S encrypts viewer traffic. If enabled, A W S vaaf filters web requests. Shield Standard provides baseline protection against denial-of-service attacks.
For a private S three bucket, Origin Access Control and the bucket policy let CloudFront fetch files without allowing direct public reads.
